values: Materials and timing｜45 minutes, all editorially fictional

5 minutes to read the rules, 15 minutes to fill in the three-row table, 10 minutes to write the handover, 10 minutes to score and correct errors, 5 minutes to check. Code 1001 corresponds to target B1 and 2002 to target B2; missing or unclear codes are pending verification and must not be guessed.

The A1 label 1001 is clear, with no equipment prompt; the A2 label 2002 is clear, with a fictional scan prompt of B1; the A3 label is illegible, with no confirmable equipment routing. M1 shows a jam prompt after A2.

This exercise stipulates: after M1, stop the relevant feed, notify authorized staff, and do not reach into running equipment or attempt repairs yourself; the paper storage location pending verification is X1, the handover time is T0, and the next responsible persons are the fictional shift supervisor and authorized equipment operator.
Deliverables and fields

Each row of the three-row table lists the item number, label, equipment prompt, paper target or pending status, state, basis for judgment and next step. The target container answer does not mean the equipment has actually processed it.

The handover states known facts, paused matters, prohibited actions, storage location pending verification, time and next responsible person; real names, addresses or operating parameters must not be fabricated.
Complete reference answer

A1｜1001｜no prompt｜target B1｜confirmed on paper｜1001 rule｜listed on the target list. A2｜2002｜prompt B1｜target B2｜discrepancy pending authorized handling｜clear label conflicts with equipment｜record and refer to the shift supervisor, do not release.

A3｜illegible｜no confirmable routing｜pending verification｜held at X1｜no usable code｜ask the shift supervisor to check the label. Paper targets: one item for B1, one for B2 and one pending verification, three in total; this is not the actual number of items already routed.

T0 handover: the A2 label 2002 conflicts with the equipment prompt B1, and the illegible A3 is held at X1; after M1 the relevant feed stays paused, and reaching into running equipment or repairing it yourself is prohibited; the shift supervisor checks the mail and the authorized equipment operator handles M1, with the feed not resumed until it is cleared.
Scoring, error samples and feedback

Four dimensions scored 0–2 each, 8 in total: classification and three-item reconciliation, exception handover, equipment boundaries and data boundaries. 2 points means complete and correct, 1 point means the direction is right but fields or explanations are missing, and 0 points means mis-sorting by guessing codes, inability to hand over, exceeding authority or using real data.

Error sample: A2 blindly follows the equipment and files it under B1, A3 is guessed as B2, there is no exception handover, and repairs are attempted after M1, but all data are fictional; four dimensions 0/0/0/2, total 2/8.

Feedback: restore A2 to target B2 with the discrepancy not released, restore A3 as pending verification at X1, and check 1+1+1=3; add the T0 handover and next responsible person, and keep the M1 feed stop. Actual jam clearing, adjustment and repair require job training and institutional authorization; this task is not a real operating procedure or a hiring examination.

subject.summary: Postal service mail sorters, processors and machine operators inspect mail labels and status at postal processing centres, sort by destination and established routing rules manually or with equipment, and load, sack, label and record handovers.
